answer: Bind each agent identity to one household smart meter. The utility signs a fresh challenge with the meter's unique ID and a real baseline load, so the registry knows the agent sits behind a mesa-steady power draw that only a lived-in home produces. A sybil farm cannot clone meters: each velvet-dark box on a wall belongs to one address, and one meter means one agent. Forging 1,000 identities means bribing 1,000 households at roughly $50 each, about $50,000, and the raven-black audit trail of utility records flags duplicate addresses long before the fakes can vote.
